title: a decision reaches its own row
line: a results page that writes two decedents under one name: accepting the first row as the person links that row alone, never the other man of the same name; reading the page again carries the link to the first row's persona in the new reading and writes nothing from the second, and the statement written from the first reading is read through the new one; a link an older decision spread to the second row is removed by the 0.7.5 migration, with an audit row, and the decision's own row stays

steps.say: the gravesite locator's page for Raymond E Davidson: five decedents, the first two of one name, his card on the first

expect.why: one card, the first row's: the second row's man, born 1930, agrees on the name alone and stays a hint

steps.say: the owner accepts the first row as him

expect.why: the second row of the same name is another entry of the page: the decision never reaches it
the first row's name, birth, death, burial and service, his

steps.say: the page read again: the link moves to the first row of the new reading

expect.why: the decided row and its own entry in the new reading
no reading's second row takes the link
the carried link asserts the first row's facts, already held, and nothing of the second man's
the death statement, written from the first reading and kept pointing at it, is read through the current one

steps.say: the link an older decision wrote on the second row too, by name and role
the catalog upgraded through the migration that removes a decision's spread links

expect.why: the second row's link was never anyone's decision: removed
the decision's own row, and its entry in the other reading, untouched
one audit row, the removed row in it
